neighbours.label: introducing an added difficulty with the words complicate/complication/difficult/harder: 'to complicate matters further', 'to make things even more difficult', 'a further complication is'; the simplify/easier twins and plain 'difficult'/'complicated' as descriptions do not fire
fire: To complicate things further, the ferry timetable changes on public holidays.
Making matters more difficult, the only bridge into town was closed for repairs.
To make it even harder, the instructions were printed only in Finnish.
The real complication is that the two databases use different customer IDs.
Things were complicated further by a strike at the port.
To make matters more difficult, the grant money arrives in a different currency.
A further complication arose when the lead actor fell ill a week before opening.
To complicate the picture, the earlier survey counted part-time staff as well.
quiet: To simplify things, the ferry timetable is the same every day of the year.
Making matters easier, a second bridge into town opened last month.
To make it simpler, the instructions were printed in four languages.
The real advantage is that the two databases share the same customer IDs.
The difficult climb took the group most of the morning.
The grant application form was long and complicated.
The lead actor recovered in time for a difficult opening night.
The earlier survey was simpler, counting only full-time staff.

predictions: Fire items 0.5-0.9 peaking on 'licate', ' difficult', ' complication' or ' harder'; simplify/easier twins 0.1-0.25, descriptive difficult/complicated under 0.15. 'To simplify matters' (0.239 in the probe) is the near miss most likely to leak.
